column1: # Outer profile of the bell of a Kruspe F/B-flat double horn, last 85 mm to the rim: READ FROM PHOTOGRAPHS, NOT A MEASURED TABLE.
# Source: Eduard Kruspe, Double Horn in F / B-flat, 1904-19, brass and nickel-silver, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, object 503607 (public domain; the museum's API records the stated dimensions

#   'Height 41.9 cm, Diameter (of bell) 31.4 cm', the diameter as 31.432564 cm). Images https://images.metmuseum.org/CRDImages/mi/original/DP-12679-153.jpg and DP-12679-154.jpg (4000 x 3963 px each; the
#   front and back of the instrument; the bell is seen from the side with its rim almost edge-on).

# Method [R]: silhouette = pixels of HSV saturation above a threshold (brass against a grey ground), closed, largest component, holes filled (the lane's bell_mask.py, not committed). The two rim tips are the lowest silhouette

#   point and the extreme point on the other side; the rim line between them is 2033.7 px (front) and 2034.2 px (back) and is SET TO the museum's stated bell diameter 314.3 mm, which gives 0.1545 mm/px

#   (the lane's bell_profile.py, not committed). The bell axis is the rim line's normal; at each axial distance z from the rim the width of the silhouette along the rim direction is the OUTER diameter. Six extractions: two views,
#   saturation thresholds 0.15, 0.22 and 0.30. Interpolated to z = 0, 5, 10 ... mm.

# Checks: the front and back views agree within 1.2 mm for z = 20 to 90 mm (largest 2.1 mm at z = 10 mm). THE SCALE RESTS ON ONE NUMBER: the museum's stated height 41.9 cm does not match the photograph at that scale (the silhouette

#   is 3415 px tall = 527.6 mm, 26 percent more) and is unexplained. An independent modern horn's printed point, the Alexander double horn of the Edinburgh University Collection (MIMEd 15417, read 2026-11-09: 114 mm at 74.5 mm from the
#   bell end), is 5 percent above this profile at z = 74.5 mm (108.3 mm); at the height-based scale this profile would read 86 mm there.

# Uncertainty: range of the six extractions 3 mm for z = 30 to 100 mm (about +-1.5 mm), 7 mm at z = 20, 13 mm at z = 10; z = 0, 5 and 15 mm met a second run of the silhouette on the measuring line (the rolled rim); z > 90 mm is not

#   readable (another tube touches the line). The wall (about 0.3 to 0.5 mm) is not subtracted: inside diameters are 0.6 to 1.0 mm smaller. THIS IS ANOTHER HORN'S BELL: no Schmid bell picture or scan was found in open form.
# Columns: z_from_rim_mm; outer_diameter_mm_mean_of_6; min_of_6; max_of_6; primary_view_t0.22; back_view_t0.22; runs_on_line_max; note.
